draft.change: Add the Syriac spelling יִהֻודָֿא as a name article linked to the same root as the Hebrew יְהוּדָה.
draft.definition: The Syriac form of the personal name Judah, borne here by Jacob’s son.
draft.evidence: Matthew 1:3 names Judah as the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Genesis 29:35 connects his Hebrew name with Leah’s declaration that she will praise Yahweh.

analysis.evidence: יִהֻודָֿא stands before אַולֵדֿ, “fathered.” The two names that follow, לפַֿרצ וַלזַרח, identify his sons, and מֵנ תָּמָר names their mother. The genealogy then continues with Perez as the next father.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, unprefixed and unsuffixed, serving as the subject of אַולֵדֿ.
analysis.sense: Judah, the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar.

analysis.evidence: Judah is the subject of אַולֵדֿ. The ל־ before Perez and Zerah marks them as the children he fathered, and מֵנ תָּמָר identifies Tamar as their mother.
analysis.morphology: Aphel perfect, third person masculine singular

analysis.evidence: Judah fathers לפַֿרצ וַלזַרח, Perez and Zerah, by Tamar. The next clause repeats the name without the prefix as פַּרצ and identifies him as Hezron’s father.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper name with prefixed ל marking the direct object of אַולֵדֿ.
analysis.sense: Perez, son of Judah and Tamar

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Zerah linked to the root article zarach.
draft.definition: The personal name Zerah, borne here by a son of Judah and Tamar.
draft.evidence: Matthew 1:3 names Zerah alongside Perez as a son of Judah by Tamar.

evidence.note: The Peshitta coordinates זַרח with Perez as the second object of ‘fathered’.
The related Hebrew noun describes the dawning of light.

article.name: זַרח
article.note: Matthew gives the family relationship without explaining the name's origin.
article.summary: Matthew names Zerah and Perez as sons of Judah by Tamar. Zerah's name shares its consonants with the Hebrew noun זֶרַח ‘dawning’.

conflicts: resolve the bearer and validate its name article against the current lexicon

analysis.evidence: The ל־ appears on both לפַרצ and וַלזַרח, pairing Perez and Zerah as the sons Judah fathered. מֵנ תָּמָר identifies Tamar as their mother.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with prefixed וַ־ ‘and’ and ל־ marking the direct object of אַולֵדֿ ‘fathered’.
analysis.sense: Zerah, son of Judah and Tamar and brother of Perez.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article linked to the תמר root article.
draft.definition: Tamar is the woman who bore Perez and Zerah to Judah.
draft.evidence: Mat.1.3 names Tamar after both sons. Rut.4.12 likewise identifies Tamar as the woman who bore Perez to Judah.

evidence.note: The Syriac names both sons before מֵנ תָּמָר, “by Tamar.”
The blessing recalls Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah.
The speaker describes climbing a תָמָר and taking hold of its fruit stalks, illustrating the palm-tree noun that gives the name its meaning.

article.name: תָּמָר
article.summary: The name Tamar has the same form as the Hebrew noun תָּמָר, “date palm.” In Matthew’s genealogy, Tamar is the mother of Judah’s sons Perez and Zerah.

conflicts: resolve the bearer and validate its name article against the current lexicon

analysis.evidence: In Mat.1.3, Judah is the subject of אַולֵדֿ, “fathered.” After naming both sons, the phrase מֵנ תָּמָר, “by Tamar,” identifies their mother.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular personal name, governed by the separate preposition מֵנ, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Tamar, the mother of Perez and Zerah

analysis.evidence: Judah fathers Perez and Zerah by Tamar. The next clause repeats Perez’s name as its subject: פַּרצ אַולֵדֿ לחֵצרָונ, “Perez fathered Hezron.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper name, subject of אַולֵדֿ, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Perez, son of Judah and Tamar

analysis.evidence: In פַּרצ אַולֵדֿ לחֵצרָונ, Perez is the subject and ל־ marks Hezron as the object. The clause says that Perez fathered Hezron.
analysis.morphology: Aphel perfect, third person masculine singular

analysis.evidence: In פַּרצ אַולֵדֿ לחֵצרָונ, Perez fathers Hezron. The next clause repeats Hezron’s name without ל as the subject who fathers Ram.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with prefixed ל marking the direct object of אַולֵדֿ ‘fathered’.
analysis.sense: Hezron, son of Perez and father of Ram.

analysis.evidence: After Perez fathers Hezron, the genealogy repeats Hezron’s name as the subject of חֵצרֻונ אַולֵדֿ לָארָמ, “Hezron fathered Ram.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, unprefixed and unsuffixed, serving as the subject of אַולֵדֿ.
analysis.sense: Hezron, son of Perez and father of Ram.

analysis.evidence: In חֵצרֻונ אַולֵדֿ לָארָמ, Hezron is the subject, and ל marks Aram as the object. The clause identifies Hezron as Aram’s father.
analysis.morphology: Aphel perfect, third person masculine singular

draft.change: Add the pointed Syriac name אָרָמ and document its correspondence to Hebrew רָם in this genealogy.
draft.definition: The Syriac personal name Aram, borne here by Hezron’s son Ram.
draft.evidence: Matthew 1:3 places Aram after Hezron in the genealogy. Ruth 4:18–19 gives the same succession from Perez through Hezron to Ram.

evidence.note: חֵצרֻונ אַולֵדֿ לָארָמ means “Hezron fathered Aram.”
Perez fathers Hezron, and Hezron fathers רָם.

article.name: אָרָמ
article.summary: The Peshitta names Hezron’s son אָרָמ in Matthew’s genealogy. Ruth calls him רָם in the Hebrew genealogy.

conflicts: resolve the bearer and validate its name article against the current lexicon

analysis.evidence: In חֵצרֻונ אַולֵדֿ לָארָמ, “Hezron fathered Aram,” the ל marks the child, just as it marks Hezron in the preceding clause, “Perez fathered Hezron.” Ruth 4:19 calls this son of Hezron רָם (Ram).
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with prefixed ל marking the direct object of אַולֵדֿ.
